name: Western Digital Corp.
reason: HDD storage is a boom-bust hardware cycle: EBIT margin 35.6% is at the 10y high (100th pctile vs 10.4% avg) with EPS 0.92x the 10y peak after losses in 2023-24, so earnings are near a cyclical peak.

name: Atlantic Union Bankshares Corp.
reason: Growth has come from acquiring other banks (shares +11.1%/yr over 10y), ROE averages only 8.1%, and EPS is 0.97x the 10y peak; an ordinary spread lender.

name: Columbia Banking System, Inc.
reason: Growth came from M&A (shares +15.4%/yr, Umpqua deal), ROE averages 8.7%, and EPS has grown only 5.4%/yr over 10y; a rate-sensitive regional bank with nothing special.

name: Becton, Dickinson & Co.
reason: Durable med-tech franchise, but growth is acquisition-driven (acquisitions 0.93x 10y FCF, ROIC 3.7%), net debt/EBITDA is 3.4x, adjusted EPS runs 73% above GAAP, the business is being reshaped by the Biosciences/Diagnostics separation, and LTG consensus is -1.7%.

name: Omnicom Group, Inc.
reason: Steady past record (EPS up 7%/yr, margin about 15%), but the newly closed IPG merger makes this a recent transformation, and generative AI is a credible threat to agency creative and media-buying economics within 5 years; revenue grew only 1.3%/yr.

name: Principal Financial Group, Inc.
reason: Earnings depend on markets and rates (fee-based AUM, retirement spreads, life insurance), EPS is at the 10y peak (1.0x), and adjusted EPS runs 33% above GAAP.

name: WaFd, Inc.
reason: A thrift-style lender with a heavy mortgage/CRE mix, so earnings follow the rate cycle (EPS fell 33% in 2024); ROE averages 9.2%.

name: Bread Financial Holdings, Inc.
reason: Private-label card lender whose earnings follow consumer credit losses (EPS swung from 18.1 to 4.5 to 14.7); 10y EPS CAGR 0.1% and revenue falling 3.1%/yr, with late-fee regulatory risk.

name: Tenet Healthcare Corp.
reason: Hospital and ASC operator dependent on government reimbursement (Medicaid/ACA subsidy cuts); EBIT margin 16.1% is at the 10y high (100th pctile vs 10.1% avg) and EPS is at the peak, with 10y avg ROE negative.

name: Simmons First National Corp.
reason: Low-return regional bank (10y avg ROE 5.7%) that diluted shareholders through acquisitions (shares +9.1%/yr); EPS has grown 0.8%/yr over 10y and is 0.68x its peak.

name: SLM Corp.
reason: Private student-loan lender driven by credit and rate cycles plus federal student-lending policy risk; EPS is 0.94x the 10y peak and consensus LTG is 4.7%.

name: Lithia Motors, Inc.
reason: Roll-up auto dealer: acquisitions total 41x 10y FCF, net debt/EBITDA is 8.1x, and EPS is 25% below the 2022 peak as used-car and gross-profit-per-unit tailwinds normalize.

name: Bunge Global SA
reason: Agricultural commodity processor whose earnings follow crush margins and crop cycles (EBIT margin 1.5%, EPS 0.54x peak); net debt/EBITDA 7.7x after the Viterra deal.

name: Crane NXT Co.
reason: Cash-payment validation and banknote security face secular decline in cash use; EPS is 0.95x the 10y peak, and growth leans on acquisitions (0.74x 10y FCF) while revenue is shrinking 4.9%/yr.

name: Ball Corp.
reason: Commodity-like aluminum can maker with 5.4% average ROIC and 0.42 FCF conversion; EBIT margin 12.7% is at the 10y high (100th pctile), and the share count was cut using aerospace divestiture proceeds, not organic growth.

name: Alamo Group, Inc.
reason: Solid but ordinary roll-up of ag and municipal equipment makers (acquisitions 0.66x 10y FCF, ROIC 9.3%); EPS is down 18% from the 2023 peak in a cyclical end market, and there is no special moat.

name: Hormel Foods Corp.
reason: Branded protein business in decline: EPS has grown 0.4%/yr over 10y and is 0.72x its peak, EBIT margin is at the 9th pctile of its history, and it is exposed to hog/turkey costs and GLP-1 volume risk.

name: Boyd Gaming Corp.
reason: Regional casinos: EBIT margin stepped up after Covid (21-28% vs 14% before) and EPS is at the peak, while consensus LTG is -12.5% and consumer-discretionary and online-gaming risks make the high margins fragile.

name: Best Buy Co., Inc.
reason: Electronics retailer with flat revenue (+0.5%/yr) and a thin 4.2% EBIT margin under Amazon/vendor-direct competition; EPS is 0.64x the 2021 peak and growth relies on buybacks.

name: Ford Motor Co.
reason: Cyclical automaker with 2.4% average ROIC and 1.4% EBIT margin; net debt/EBITDA is 14.9x (captive finance), the EV transition and tariffs make earnings unforecastable, and EPS has fallen 5.6%/yr over 10y.
